olivia (support): Customer report: credits didn't decrement for several streaming chat requests after client retried. Account: acct_9982. Customer says UI still shows full trial balance even after successful messages. sample req id: req_20260302_abc

olivia (support): Repro steps from customer:
1) Start streaming chat via websocket/HTTP chunking.
2) Client loses connection on chunk 2, retries by re-opening a new stream and resending prompt.
3) Conversation completes, UI shows messages but balance unchanged.

olivia (support): Attached API logs they pasted:
```
[2026-03-02T15:10:05Z] REQUEST req_20260302_abc idempotency-key=null headers:{Authorization: Bearer x, X-Client-Version: 1.2}
[2026-03-02T15:10:08Z] STREAM_CHUNK req_20260302_abc chunk=1 tokens=42
[2026-03-02T15:10:09Z] CONNECTION_RESET by client
[2026-03-02T15:10:10Z] REQUEST req_20260302_def idempotency-key=abcd-1234 headers:{Authorization: Bearer x}
[2026-03-02T15:10:11Z] STREAM_CHUNK req_20260302_def chunk=1 tokens=42
[2026-03-02T15:10:12Z] STREAM_END req_20260302_def tokens_total=820
[2026-03-02T15:10:12Z] BILLING_DEBIT acct_9982 amount=0 tokens=0 reason: (no debit)
```

rajiv (eng-runtime): Quick q — was the client adding an idempotency key on retry? Looks like first request had none, retry had a fresh key. That would bypass dedup semantics.

olivia (support): Customer confirms their client did NOT preserve idempotency-key across reconnection. They assumed server dedupes by user/session.

rajiv (eng-runtime): That explains it. For streaming we only finalize token debit when we see a terminal STREAM_END associated with a request id. If retries open a new request id without the original idempotency-key, server treats it as a distinct session. If the first stream was aborted after partial compute we don't always roll back internal counters — edge case: partial compute got tallied but we didn't persist a debit because STREAM_END never fired, leading to ledger inconsistency.

billing-qa: Ledger snapshot shows no debit for acct_9982 between 15:09-15:11, but there are two internal compute jobs logged. We need invoice ids to trace.

olivia (support): Invoice ids posted by customer: invoice_local_443 and invoice_local_444 (they're customer-side IDs). Backend request ids: req_20260302_abc and req_20260302_def.

support-bot: Created escalation ticket INC-4567 and linked billing case BILL-7892 

rajiv (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate mitigation: enforce server-side idempotency by honoring a new header X-stream-session-id if present — treat repeated session ids as same logical request and only debit once when STREAM_END arrives. Will open a bug: RINF-3241.

eva (product): Can we also add a safe fallback: when connection is reset and a retry starts within 30s with the same client auth token, mark compute as potentially dedupable and hold final debit until operator confirms? Need tradeoffs vs delayed billing.

rajiv (eng-runtime): I'll scope RINF-3241: 1) ensure idempotency-key persisted across LB restarts, 2) introduce stream_session_id support, 3) prevent double-debits by only writing to billing ledger on STREAM_END commit path. ETA: patch + canary in 5 business days.

billing-qa: For this customer we'll issue a one-time 50-credit adjustment pending root cause. will post adjustment id here when done.

olivia (support): I told customer we'll credit them 50 while we investigate and asked for anything else (sdk version, proxy config). They sent back that they're using sdk-js v0.9.2 and a corporate proxy that tears sockets on idle.

rajiv (eng-runtime): Action items:
- rajiv: create RINF-3241 and PR for stream_session_id (in progress)
- rajiv: add logs to track when STREAM_END missing but compute ran
- billing-qa: apply adjustment and confirm
- olivia: send customer interim credit and repro checklist (sdk version, proxy)

olivia (support): Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer and keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
